- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Reform UK 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Overview

Reform UK's manifesto presents itself as a "Contract" outlining policy proposals across multiple areas, with detailed costings claiming £150 billion in annual savings and £141 billion in annual costs, plus £10 billion in projected additional tax revenue from economic growth.

## Immigration Policy

The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and implementing offshore processing for asylum seekers. Foreign workers would face a 20% National Insurance rate (versus 13.8% for British workers), with exemptions for healthcare workers and small businesses. A five-year residency requirement would apply before accessing benefits. Student visa holders would be barred from bringing dependents.

## Economic Proposals

**Personal taxation:** Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 (from current levels), keeping the basic rate at 20% with higher rate starting at £70,000. Stamp duty would be eliminated below £750,000. Inheritance tax would be abolished for estates under £2 million.

**Business measures:** Corporation tax would drop from 25% to 15% over time, with businesses under £100,000 profit exempt. VAT threshold would rise to £150,000. Business rates would be abolished for high-street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals. IR35 rules would be abolished.

## Government Spending

Proposed savings include: stopping Bank of England interest payments on QE reserves (£35 billion), 5% efficiency cuts across departments (£50 billion), halving foreign aid (£6 billion), and scrapping HS2 (£25 billion one-off).

## Healthcare

NHS reforms include tax exemptions for frontline staff, 20% tax relief on private healthcare, and a voucher system allowing patients to access private care if NHS waiting times exceed specified limits (3 days for GPs, 3 weeks for consultants, 9 weeks for operations). Student loan write-offs would be offered for medical staff completing 10 years of NHS service.

## Energy Policy

The manifesto proposes scrapping net zero commitments and renewable energy subsidies, fast-tracking North Sea oil and gas licensing, granting shale gas test licences, and developing small modular nuclear reactors. Environmental levies and VAT on energy bills would be removed, claiming £500 annual savings per household.

## Law and Order

Police numbers would increase by 40,000 officers over five years. Proposals include mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders, 10,000 new prison places, and changes to hate crime definitions. Foreign criminals would face immediate deportation after serving sentences.

## Education

Policies include banning gender identity teaching in schools, 20% tax relief on private school fees (explicitly rejecting VAT on fees), scrapping student loan interest, and reducing undergraduate numbers while enforcing minimum entry standards. Universities failing to protect free speech would face funding cuts.

## Benefits

A "2-strike rule" would withdraw benefits from those refusing two job offers within four months. Face-to-face assessments would replace remote evaluations for disability benefits, with exemptions for severe conditions.

## Brexit and Sovereignty

The party would repeal retained EU laws, abandon the Windsor Framework governing Northern Ireland arrangements, and withdraw from EU defence programmes. Renegotiation of the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement is proposed.

## Defence

Military spending would increase to 3% of GDP within six years. Pay increases for armed forces personnel are proposed, along with a new veterans department. The manifesto opposes military national service, instead advocating recruiting 30,000 full-time army personnel.

## Housing

Planning reforms would fast-track brownfield development. Section 24 landlord tax restrictions would be scrapped, and the Renters Reform Bill would be abolished. Social housing allocation would prioritise British nationals with longer residency.

## Constitutional Changes

Proposals include leaving the ECHR, reforming the House of Lords, restricting postal voting, and holding a referendum on proportional representation. The BBC licence fee would be abolished.

## Other Policies

- Marriage tax allowance of 25% transferable between spouses
- Farming budget increased to £3 billion with focus on smaller farms
- Fishing industry reforms including licensing fees for foreign vessels
- Royal Commission on social care
- Rejection of WHO Pandemic Treaty and central bank digital currencies
